lines.x: Asian stocks plummeted on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 sinking 5.1% and South Korea's Kospi tumbling 5.2%.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament that the central bank should continue raising interest rates to keep underlying inflation anchored near its 2% target.

Japan's economy shrank by an annualised 0.1% in the July-September quarter, marking its first contraction in four quarters as persistent inflation and elevated living costs weighed on private consumption.
SoftBank Group CEO Masayoshi Son has reportedly approached Wall Street institutions to discuss financing a potential $1 trillion buyout of South Korean memory chip manufacturer SK Hynix.
